## Purpose

title: [ROCm][Perf] W4A16: pad gfx11 weight and activation strides
body:
On gfx11 (RDNA3/3.5) a W4A16 GEMM loses a large share of its achievable read bandwidth when an operand's row stride lands on a multiple of 1024 bytes. The rows alias into the same L2/DDR channels and the accesses serialize. Offsetting the stride by one 128 B cache line dodges it.

This PR nudges **both** operands off that cliff: the packed weight row (padded once at load) and the activation row (padded per call) and improves TTFT by up to 23 % and TPOT by up to 3 %.
Padding the activation (at runtime) pays for itself due to reduced GEMM time.

## The two cliffs

For weights, we pad at load time when they are a multiple of 1024 bytes. For activations,
we only pad when they are a multiple of 2048 bytes to ensure that their cost is recovered by the GEMM wins.

Cherry-pick of #36811 (main commit 221a6273ce) onto `qwen4-main-squashed`. One trivial conflict resolved: this branch still had the `assert bias.dtype == torch.float32` line that #36811 deletes.

On DGX Spark (GB10) every NEXTN cell of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 built from this branch sporadically collapses to repeated `!` (NaN logits, #37111). > `handle_attention_aiter` can return `MHA_CHUNKED_KV`.

## Motivation

Speculative decoding for MLA models is unreachable on the aiter backend on
CDNA3. aiter's asm MLA selects a kernel from a fixed table, and on gfx942 that
table has no entry for the shapes Kimi-K3 needs:

- **12 query heads.** Kimi-K3 at TP8 is 96/8 = 12 per rank; aiter requires 4, 8,
  or a multiple of 16 in [16, 128]. `AiterAttnBackend`'s head padding does not
  reach it either — `head_repeat_factor = 16 // 12 = 1`, so nothing is repeated

title: [Perf][Model Loader] Fault in mmap'd weight pages before host-to-device copies on integrated GPUs
body:
## Purpose

Addresses #58726.

On integrated GPUs (DGX Spark / GB10), the shared weight loaders copy each checkpoint tensor to the GPU with `param.copy_(loaded_weight)` straight from the safetensors mmap view. For a contiguous, same-dtype source, PyTorch passes that pageable pointer directly to the driver copy, so the page faults happen inside the copy. On GB10 that is several times slower than faulting the same pages on the CPU first: 1.7–3.0 ms vs 0.08–0.64 ms per 800 KiB tensor in #58726. `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` has at least 140k such tensors, and its main weight load takes 452 s from NFS and 475 s from local NVMe.

# fix(moe): correct fused shared-expert scaling on aiter/DeepEP path

## Motivation

On the HIP aiter + DeepEP-class MoE path (e.g. MoRI all-to-all), the fused shared
expert is under-weighted by `routed_scaling_factor`, corrupting every MoE layer
and producing degenerate, non-converging generation on long outputs.

Two code paths scale the MoE output differently:
